answer.rationale: The recovered archive records expose a consolidation drift problem: memory_73 states targeted promotional pricing produced 'strong acquisition and revenue lift', but its source record exp_73 shows signup +31% and qualified revenue +18% alongside 30-day retention -12%, with an explicit source-level instruction NOT to generalize discounting as sustainable growth. The consolidated memory dropped the retention loss and the warning. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, promotional_pricing is therefore the one direction the evidence actively argues against, even though it is the most tempting reflex against a competitor price cut — matching a deeper discount would buy a cohort that does not survive first renewal, worsening the very SMB churn we are reacting to. By contrast, memory_86 is corroborated by its own source (exp_86: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, 30-day retention +3%) — it is the only direction with verified retention-positive evidence, which is exactly the lever that addresses churn rather than masking it. memory_31 points the same way (signup simplification lifting SMB activation) and is directionally consistent, but it is unverified this cycle, so I lean on it only as supporting, not load-bearing. The remaining memories (memory_91 activation messaging, memory_57 referrals, memory_44 enterprise sales-assist) are plausible but share the same unverified consolidation pathway that demonstrably lost critical caveats in memory_73; I will not build a crisis response on them and have queued them for verification. Because one confirmed drift implies the archive's summarization is systematically lossy on harm signals, I scope this as a standard experiment on the self-serve SMB segment with retention (not just activation/completion) as a gating metric, rather than a broad rollout. Downstream risk flagged: onboarding improvements do not directly neutralize a price gap, so churn conversations may continue near-term and leadership should not read this as a full competitive answer; if retention does not hold, revisit next cycle with restored verification budget.
